Product Development and Adoption

01 · Advertising Campaign Automation

Ticket-to-Campaign

BRD authoring Requirements Global adoption
Workflow proof point: marketer submits a TTC ticket; the system validates inputs, generates campaign structure, creates the campaign in Meta, and returns launch-ready status.

Problem

Campaign setup was manual, fragmented across tools, and difficult to scale globally. This slowed revenue-driving launches, limited peak-event scale, and made it harder to standardize campaign quality across markets.

My Role

  • Identified the campaign setup problem through hands-on marketing work and owned requirements and rollout with technical partners.
  • Defined the BRD, requirements, roadmap, UAT plan, and launch readiness; translated the workflow into practical guidance for marketers.
  • Led worldwide enablement through training materials, demos, and office hours, helping country teams understand where and how to use the product.
  • Partnered on API dependencies, product set/feed logic, QA integration, and workflow design.

Business Impact

The 2025 MVP supported 28 campaigns. In 2026, the capability expanded to 23 countries, with enablement focused on adoption in everyday campaign workflows.

02 · Campaign Validation

Ad Configuration QA

Product vision Rule logic Dashboard
Dashboard proof point: centralized view of QA status, rule checks, and violations across Social Marketing ads.

Problem

Campaign QA relied on manual peer review, creating inconsistent standards, launch delays, and limited visibility into setup or policy violations—especially risky during high-visibility events like Prime Day.

My Role

  • Authored product vision and BRD for automated campaign validation.
  • Defined requirements for continuous monitoring, front card checks, HVE validation, exceptions, and dashboard visibility.
  • Partnered with engineering on rule logic, data requirements, TTC integration, UAT, and Prime Day readiness.

Impact

Launch qualityReduce risk of misconfigured ads before activation
HVE readinessSupport Prime Day rules like overlays and front cards

How I Bring New Capabilities to Users

Understand the workflow

Start with the user's task and friction points. Use operating experience and stakeholder feedback to define the problem, scope, and success criteria.

Make the value concrete

Connect features to a practical use case. Create demos and training that explain what the product does, when to use it, and what still requires human judgment.

Support adoption

Pair launch readiness with live enablement and office hours. Bring questions and workflow gaps back into conversations about priorities and improvements.
